Subject: Control alignment & timeline questions for upcoming FedRAMP/ISO work

Diego / Marissa —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. RedPine's security team is finalizing the scope for our integration and we want to align on a few items before we lock dates with procurement and our external assessor:

1) For FedRAMP scoping: do you plan to pursue FedRAMP Low initially or go straight for Moderate? Our assessor needs to know expected control baselines to size the pre-audit evidence request.

2) ISO 27001: we heard you have a 3-phase plan (gap remediation, pre-cert internal audit, external audit). Can you share the target months for each phase and the approximate list of control owners we should engage?

3) Evidence cadence: what's your preferred delivery format (Drive folder + spreadsheet tracker vs. platform upload)? We typically supply a 60-day sampling window; will that work for token/log samples?

Attached: proposed evidence template from our side for initial mapping.

Can we do a short sync Tues or Wed? Times work best for our team 10:00–12:00 ET.

Appreciate it —
Sarah
Sarah Mills
Security & Compliance Lead, RedPine Health

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control alignment & timeline questions for upcoming FedRAMP/ISO work

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear ask and the template. Short answers up-front, then a proposed plan.

- FedRAMP baseline: we are targeting FedRAMP Low initially with a parallel path to Moderate over the next 9–12 months. Low is the default for most customers integrating in Q3; Moderate will require some infra changes (enhanced encryption key separation and host-level hardening) that we can accelerate for prioritized partners.

- ISO 27001 phases (high level):
  * Phase A (gap remediation): June–August 2027 — remediation of identified documented gaps from our internal assessment.
  * Phase B (internal/pre-cert audit): September 2027.
  * Phase C (external audit/certification): Q4 2027 (target October/November).

Control owners: I am attaching our current control matrix (redwood_control_matrix_v1.xlsx). Primary owners for controls relevant to your scope will be: Marissa (compliance processes & evidence), Mina (security controls, logging, access), and Infrastructure/Platform (owner list in the matrix).

Evidence cadence and format: we prefer a shared Drive folder keyed to the evidence-request-template (attached: evidence-request-template.xlsx). That lets us map files to control IDs and track sampling. For log/token sampling, 60-day windows are fine; we suggest a combined approach:
  - Provide full artifact files (policies, architecture diagrams) in Drive.
  - Use the spreadsheet to record file mappings and sample ranges.
  - For large log exports we can provide filtered extracts and a small verification script to reproduce the filters.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick sync Wed May 12 10:30–11:00 ET (I will send a calendar invite).
2) We will drop the Drive folder and populate initial artifacts + the control matrix by EOD May 11.
3) Marissa and Mina will own the first evidence pull and follow the sampling windows you specify.

I attached the control matrix and the evidence template so you can review and indicate any missing fields.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Director, Strategic Accounts (Americas) — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_control_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 240KB), evidence-request-template.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45KB)

Sarah / Diego —

Adding a bit more color from the compliance side so your assessor has actionable items for scoping:

- FedRAMP Low vs Moderate: If RedPine can confirm Moderate is a future requirement, we will prioritize HSM-backed key separation, host hardening baselines, and some network segmentation changes. Estimate to enable Moderate-ready state (software + infra changes) is ~12 weeks once prioritized.

- ISO control owners: in the attached matrix we include owner emails. For your convenience the primary contacts for evidence pulls are:
  * marissa_cole@redwood.ai — process policies, training records, vendor assessments
  * mina_haddad@redwood.ai — technical configs, logging/monitoring extracts, IAM evidence
  * infra-ops@redwood.ai (alias) — host-level hardening and patching records

- Sampling & evidence windows: for ISO audits we typically provide 90-day windows for operational controls and 30–60 days for change controls. For FedRAMP assessments the assessor will ask for 90 days for certain continuous monitoring artifacts; please confirm if your assessor has a preferred sample window and we'll adapt.

I can join tomorrow's sync and bring a short checklist for the assessor (audit-ready artifact list).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@redpinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control alignment & timeline questions for upcoming FedRAMP/ISO work

Quick technical notes for the auditor and RedPine security team:

- SOC 2 evidence: we have a rolling Type II window (Jan–Dec 2027). The SOC 2 readiness pack includes the control evidence index and sample pulls. I can provide the SOC 2 evidence index in the Drive folder by EOD today.

- Logs & retention: our current retention policy (attached: log-retention-policy.pdf) keeps audit logs for 12 months and aggregated metrics for 36 months. For FedRAMP Moderate we will need to ensure 12+ months of immutable logs in a customer-specific retention set; that's in our Moderate roadmap.

- KMS/Encryption: keys are customer-isolated in our Dedicated/private deployments and managed through KMS with rotation policies. For hosted customers we offer provider-managed KMS with BYOK options. If RedPine needs HSM-backed attestations for Moderate, we will need to sign an addendum and kick a procurement path.

I will bring sample query outputs and a short checklist to the sync.

— Mina
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
